Where it began

Rahkeem Cornwall was born in Antigua on 1 February 1993. He played his first-class cricket for the Leeward Islands, and in 2016 he caught the eye against the touring Indians, top-scoring with 41 for a President's XI and then taking five wickets.

That autumn he went to Sri Lanka with West Indies A and took 23 wickets across three unofficial Tests at under 20 each, more than anyone else in the series. He also spent time playing club cricket in England for Thames Ditton, where he was a dangerous bowler and an occasionally destructive batsman.

The player

He bowls right-arm off-breaks and bats with real power. In 2018–19 he was the top wicket-taker in the regional four-day competition with 54 wickets from just nine matches, and that August he was named the Championship Player of the Year by Cricket West Indies. Later that month he made his Test debut, against India.

In November 2019, in a one-off Test against Afghanistan, he took his first five-wicket haul. Between 2019 and 2023 he played 10 Tests, taking 35 wickets at 37.60 with a best of 7 for 75, two five-wicket innings and one ten-wicket match. He also made two Test fifties, with a best of 73, and held 15 catches.

What made him special

Wickets, and lots of them. Only one man had taken more wickets for the Leeward Islands than him, in first-class and List A cricket alike, and he was the leading wicket-taker again in the 2022–23 West Indies Championship, with 35. With the bat he was no passenger either: only Kieran Powell made more one-day hundreds for the Leewards than his four.

In the Caribbean Premier League he once reached fifty from 26 balls after being sent in to open, his first in T20 cricket. A man who can bowl long spells and then do that is a handy one to have about.

Away from the middle

In 2017 he captained the Leeward Islands while Kieran Powell was away with the Test side, and he played in the Caribbean Premier League for the Antigua Hawksbills, St Lucia and the Barbados Royals, as well as in Minor League Cricket in the United States in 2021.

And finally

A side looking for runs at the bottom of the order, wickets in the middle and safe catching could do worse than pick him. For a long time the Leeward Islands did, and they were all the better for it.
